title: The credential temp file is created 0644 and the chmod that fixes it runs too late and can fail silently
method: replay of add_phone.py's exact write sequence with stat(2) at each step, plus source read
triggers: cura add-phone (temp-file write / os.replace / chmod sequence)

must_not_contain: carrying the Twilio auth token is created

observed_at_discovery: Replaying lines 124-131 of add_phone.py: the temp file holding the full auth token is created 0664 (0644 under umask 022); os.replace carries that mode onto the config, which is 0664 until the chmod(0o600) on the next line. Confirmed by stat: 'TMP mode at creation: 0o664', 'config mode after os.replace, BEFORE chmod: 0o664', 'config mode after chmod: 0o600'. The chmod is wrapped in `except OSError: pass`, so on any filesystem without POSIX modes -- an exFAT stick or a network home, both plausible here -- the token stays world-readable and the caregiver is told 'Phone calls are on.' pytest exit 1, 2 failed.
